judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Product-tile wrapper <div role="link"> (no href, no tabindex, not focusable) around an <article> holding the tile ("Mens Nanda Devi Insulated JacketNewMountain E..."). Under accname 1.2 (step 2H) a role=link takes its name from all descendant content, so it does have a name, though a long one. Chrome reports "" only because it does not recurse through the article role. Read fairly, the "computes no name" claim is a browser artefact. The wrapper has real problems of other kinds (a link role on a non-focusable container with nested links, which touches 2.1.1 and role semantics), but not the missing name the finding reports. Each tile also holds a properly named stretched link.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Colour-filter swatch image in the Colour facet, inside the label whose visible text is "White (207)". Its alt (and title) is "id_ffffff", the same as its src file name (id_ffffff.svg), and the browser exposes it as an image named that string (it is in the accessibility tree even while the accordion is collapsed). The swatch only repeats the colour named in the adjacent text, so it should be alt="". As coded, a screen reader reads a file name: F30 (file name as text alternative), and also not ignorable (F38/F39 style).

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Brand checkbox in the "Brands" filter facet, labelled by a visible <label for> reading "Didriksons(9)". 2.4.6 asks that labels describe topic or purpose, and in a list of brand filters a brand name with its result count says exactly what the checkbox does. A checkbox takes no entered value, so demanding that its label "say what to enter" applies a different test from the one the criterion sets.
